title: $\pi^3$: Permutation-Equivariant Visual Geometry Learning
claim: One feed-forward model reconstructs diverse open-domain scenes, and it outperforms prior methods across many geometry benchmarks.
layout: Mosaic of rounded scene panels, with a circular radar chart at bottom right
description: The figure is a dense mosaic of rounded-rectangle panels. Each panel shows a colorful 3D point-cloud reconstruction of a different scene. The scenes include a skyscraper district, a Chinese gate building, a canyon, a model train, a warehouse shelf, interiors, and a cartoon-style road. Many are dynamic: horses jumping, skaters, runners, a crowd in a corridor, and race cars. Motion is shown as repeated, overlapping figures along the trajectory. The bottom-right panel is a large circular radar chart with an outer ring split into four task sectors: camera pose, point map, video depth, and monocular depth estimation. Each sector lists dataset names such as Sintel, KITTI, ScanNet, and DTU. Four colored polygons are drawn, π³ in red and VGGT, FLARE and Fast3R in blues and greys. The red polygon encloses the others. The eye goes first to the large reconstructions, then to the radar chart.
caption: \NickName effectively reconstructs a diverse set of open-domain images in a feed-forward manner, encompassing various scenes such as indoor, outdoor, and aerial-view, as well as cartoons, with both dynamic and static content.
abstract: We introduce $Ï^3$, a feed-forward neural network that offers a novel approach to visual geometry reconstruction, breaking the reliance on a conventional fixed reference view. Previous methods often anchor their reconstructions to a designated viewpoint, an inductive bias that can lead to instability and failures if the reference is suboptimal. In contrast, $Ï^3$ employs a fully permutation-equivariant architecture to predict affine-invariant camera poses and scale-invariant local point maps without any reference frames. This design not only makes our model inherently robust to input ordering, but also leads to higher accuracy and performance. These advantages enable our simple and bias-free approach to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of tasks, including camera pose estimation, monocular/video depth estimation, and dense point map reconstruction. Code and models are available at https://github.com/yyfz/Pi3.
